views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold our current pressure posture — allow the already-ordered List 4A tariff to take effect September 1 so we do not lose negotiating credibility — but do NOT escalate further, and pivot firmly into the talks scheduled for early September. Signal conditional willingness to de-escalate (pause/roll back some tariffs) in exchange for verifiable structural commitments on IP, forced technology transfer, and purchases. The leverage is already built; the priority now is to convert it into an agreement rather than add fuel to a recession signal we ourselves are generating.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat is high but not existential (+0.5). The dispute is now materially damaging the U.S. economy and markets: the 10-year yield collapsed ~46% to 1.47% and the yield curve inverted as deeply as 2007 (country_health DGS10/DGS2), consumer sentiment fell 7.6% in a single month to 89.8 (UMCSENT), and the Dow posted its worst day of the year on Aug 14 on inversion fears (NBC/WaPo). With the Fed already easing (FEDFUNDS to 2.13) and Trump campaigning on the economy, a self-inflicted trade recession is the real enemy. Yet the U.S. holds strong leverage — 25% tariffs on ~$250B, the Huawei entity list, the currency-manipulator designation, and List 4A teed up for Sept 1 (event_timeline Aug 1/5/13/23) — so this is not a vulnerability to China but a manageable, market-sensitive escalation. That dual reading drives an action stance just above neutral (+0.1): escalation beyond the already-ordered List 4A would sharply raise recession odds and hurt our own political position, while concession now would squander hard-won leverage with no matched Chinese offer. Negotiating now, with pressure held and a credible de-escalation path on the table, is the correct calibration.
